ai.literal: Action's strength and, one's own strength and, enemy's strength and, ally's strength and, having weighed, act.
ai.translation: Weigh the strength of the deed, your own strength, the enemy's strength, and the strength of your allies, and then act.
ai.modern: செய்யப்போகும் செயலின் வலிமையையும், தன் வலிமையையும், பகைவனின் வலிமையையும், இரு தரப்பிற்கும் உள்ள துணையின் வலிமையையும் சீர்தூக்கிப் பார்த்து ஒரு செயலைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the four crucial assessments required before undertaking any action. The word 'வலி' (strength) is repeated four times to emphasize that power is multifaceted. One must evaluate the difficulty of the task itself ('வினை'), one's own capacity ('தன்'), the opponent's power ('மாற்றான்'), and the support available from allies ('துணை'). The verb 'தூக்கி' literally means 'having weighed' like on a balance scale, instructing the leader to carefully balance these four factors before acting ('செயல்').

ai.literal: What is possible, what is to be known, having known, in that abiding, to those who proceed, what does not proceed is not.
ai.translation: There is nothing impossible for those who know what is possible, know what must be known, and proceed while abiding in that knowledge.
ai.modern: தம்மால் செய்யக்கூடியது எது, அறிய வேண்டியது எது என்பதை அறிந்து, அந்த அறிவிலேயே நிலைத்து நின்று செயல்படுபவர்களுக்கு முடியாத செயல் என்று எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet explains the importance of assessing one's capabilities before acting. The word 'ஒல்வது' refers to what is practically possible for a person to achieve. By knowing this, along with other necessary knowledge, and firmly basing their actions on this understanding, a person ensures their success. For such careful individuals, there is no goal that cannot be reached.

ai.literal: Their own strength knowing not, out of zeal having started, in the middle broke down many.
ai.translation: Many have broken down midway through an undertaking, having started it out of mere zeal without knowing their own strength.
ai.modern: தமக்கு உள்ள வலிமையின் அளவை அறியாமல், வெறும் மன எழுச்சியினால் ஒரு செயலைத் தொடங்கி, அதை முடிக்க முடியாமல் இடையில் கெட்டவர்கள் பலர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against starting tasks based purely on enthusiasm without assessing one's actual capabilities. The word 'ஊக்கத்தின்' highlights that zeal alone is the driving force here, which is insufficient for success. Consequently, 'இடைக்கண் முரிந்தார்' vividly describes how such people break down or fail midway through their endeavors.

ai.literal: Having adapted in that way he behaves not; the measure he knows not; himself he admired; swiftly he will perish.
ai.translation: He who does not act in harmony with others, who is ignorant of the true measure of his own strength, and who boasts about himself, will swiftly perish.
ai.modern: மற்றவர்களுடன் ஒத்துப்போகாமல், தன் வலிமையின் அளவை அறியாமல், தன்னைத் தானே பெருமையாக நினைத்துக்கொள்பவன் விரைவில் அழிந்து போவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the rapid downfall of an arrogant and uncooperative person. The word 'அமைந்து' means adapting or acting in harmony with one's surroundings. The person described here fails to adapt ('ஒழுகான்'), does not understand the true measure of his own strength ('அளவு அறியான்'), and instead excessively admires himself ('தன்னை வியந்தான்'). Because of this toxic combination of ignorance, inflexibility, and vanity, his destruction will come swiftly.

ai.literal: Peacock feather-loaded cart even, axle will break, those goods abundantly having increased if loaded.
ai.translation: Even a cart loaded with light peacock feathers will have its axle break, if those goods are loaded in too great an excess.
ai.modern: மென்மையான மயில் இறகுகளை ஏற்றிய வண்டியாக இருந்தாலும், அந்தப் பொருளை அளவுக்கு அதிகமாக ஏற்றினால் அதன் அச்சு முறிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid metaphor to warn against underestimating the cumulative weight of small things. Peacock feathers ('பீலி') are extremely light, but if a cart ('சாகாடு') is overloaded with them, its axle ('அச்சு') will still break. In the context of knowing one's strength, it teaches that taking on too many small, seemingly easy tasks or facing too many weak enemies at once can lead to one's downfall.

ai.literal: Tip of branch they who climbed, that having exceeded if they strive, to life end having become it will leave.
ai.translation: If those who have climbed to the very tip of a branch try to push beyond it, it will result in the end of their life.
ai.modern: ஒரு மரக்கிளையின் நுனிவரை ஏறியவர்கள், அந்த எல்லையைத் தாண்டி மேலே செல்ல முயன்றால், அது அவர்களின் உயிருக்கே முடிவாகிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the vivid image of climbing a tree to illustrate the danger of overstepping one's limits. The words 'நுனி' (tip) and 'கொம்பர்' (branch) set the scene of someone who has already reached the highest possible point. If they strive ('ஊக்கின்') to go beyond ('இறந்து') that limit ('அஃது'), they will inevitably fall. It serves as a powerful metaphor for knowing the boundaries of one's power and position, warning that excessive ambition beyond one's capacity leads to ruin.

ai.literal: Of the capacity fully having known let one give; that wealth having preserved maintaining way.
ai.translation: Give to others only after fully knowing the measure of your own capacity. That is the true way to preserve and maintain your wealth.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் செல்வத்தின் அளவை முழுமையாக அறிந்து அதற்கேற்ப மற்றவர்களுக்குக் கொடுக்க வேண்டும். அதுவே அவனது செல்வத்தைப் பாதுகாத்து வாழும் வழியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises giving to others only within one's means. The word 'ஆற்றின்' refers to the measure of one's capacity or wealth, which must be fully understood ('அற அறிந்து') before giving ('ஈக'). Doing so is described as the true path ('நெறி') to safeguard ('போற்றி') and sustain one's wealth, preventing ruin through over-generosity.

ai.translation: Even if the channel of income is small, there is no harm as long as the channel of expenditure does not widen.
ai.modern: பொருள் வரும் வழி சிறியதாக இருந்தாலும், செலவு செய்யும் வழி விரிவடையாமல் இருந்தால் ஒருவருக்கு எந்தக் கேடும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet teaches the fundamental principle of living within one's means. The word 'ஆகாறு' refers to the channel of income, while 'போகாறு' refers to the channel of expenditure. The poet states that having a small income is not a cause for ruin. Financial stability is maintained as long as one's expenses do not expand beyond the limits of their wealth.

ai.literal: Measure having known he who does not live's life, existing like, having become nothing, without appearing will perish.
ai.translation: The life of one who does not live knowing the measure of his resources will seem to exist, but will become nothing and perish without a trace.
ai.modern: தன் செல்வத்தின் அளவை அறிந்து வாழாதவனின் வாழ்க்கை, இருப்பது போலத் தோன்றி, உண்மையில் இல்லாமல் ஆகி சுவடு தெரியாமல் அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against living beyond one's means. The word 'aḷavu' refers to the measure or limit of one's wealth and resources. If a person does not understand this limit and live accordingly, their life might look prosperous on the outside. However, their resources will silently drain away, and they will eventually be ruined without leaving a trace.
